cards.title: Lunchbox Harbor Spoon Ferry
cards.useCase: Use at a blanket-fort writing table when learners need dialogue that sounds like it belongs in the scene: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Read this tiny scene aloud: A spoon ferry bumps against a lunchbox dock while a sandwich sail flaps in the harbor breeze. Two helpers must trade one clear line each before the snack tide turns. Choose who speaks first: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write two short lines. Each line should mention one harbor detail, such as the spoon ferry, lunchbox dock, sandwich sail, crumb waves, or napkin flag. Line 1: ____________________ Line 2: ____________________.
cards.speakerOnePrompt: Speaker One is the Ferry Helper. Start with a line that welcomes the other helper aboard the spoon ferry. ____________________.
cards.speakerTwoPrompt: Speaker Two is the Lunchbox Lookout. Answer with a line about what they see near the dock. ____________________.
cards.dialogueTagPrompt: Add a tag after one line. Use a simple tag such as said, called, whispered, or asked. Dialogue tag: ____________________.
cards.feelingCluePrompt: Show one feeling with a tiny action instead of naming it. Example idea: tapping the napkin flag, gripping the ferry rail, or peeking over the lunchbox lid. Feeling clue: ____________________.
cards.replyPrompt: Have Speaker One reply to the lookout's news with a helpful next step. Reply: ____________________.
cards.reviseLinePrompt: Change this plain line so it sounds like harbor talk: We should go now. New line: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Point to one harbor item and write only one spoken line for it. ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: At home, add one more ferry line that includes a sound from the snack harbor. ____________________.

cards.title: Acorn Avenue Errand Desk
cards.useCase: Use when learners need practice making two fictional characters disagree kindly while solving a small errand mix-up: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Read this scene: In the Acorn Avenue Errand Office, a tiny cart of acorns has been sent to the button counter instead of the leaf stamp desk. Two office helpers must fix the mix-up without being rude. Helper roles: ____________________ and ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a polite disagreement. One helper thinks the acorns belong at the button counter. The other thinks they belong at the leaf stamp desk. Line 1: ____________________ Line 2: ____________________.
cards.speakerOnePrompt: Speaker One is the Button Counter Helper. Write a line that explains why the acorns might belong there. ____________________.
cards.speakerTwoPrompt: Speaker Two is the Leaf Stamp Helper. Disagree politely and give a reason. Use words like I think, maybe, or could we. ____________________.
cards.dialogueTagPrompt: Add one dialogue tag that shows the office voice is calm. Tag line: ____________________.
cards.feelingCluePrompt: Add a feeling clue with an office object, such as straightening a paper stack, smoothing a leaf form, or nudging the acorn cart. Feeling clue: ____________________.
cards.replyPrompt: Write a reply where the first helper accepts a fair test or plan. Reply: ____________________.
cards.reviseLinePrompt: Change this bossy line into a polite office line: No, you are wrong. New line: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle button counter or leaf stamp desk, then write one kind sentence for that helper. ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add one more errand-office line where both helpers agree on the next stop. ____________________.

cards.title: Seed Library Map Question
cards.useCase: Use when writers need to build a clear question-and-answer exchange inside a fictional map-room scene: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Read this scene: In the seed library map room, drawers of seed packets line the wall, and a giant garden map has one missing path label. Two map helpers must ask and answer before choosing where to place the path card. Missing path name: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write one question and one answer. The answer must give a useful detail from the map room. Question: ____________________ Answer: ____________________.
cards.speakerOnePrompt: Speaker One is the Map Finder. Ask about the missing path, the seed drawer, or the garden symbol. ____________________.
cards.speakerTwoPrompt: Speaker Two is the Seed Shelf Guide. Reply with one exact clue, such as a drawer color, packet symbol, or map corner. ____________________.
cards.dialogueTagPrompt: Add a dialogue tag that fits a quiet map room. Try murmured, asked, answered, or said. Tag line: ____________________.
cards.feelingCluePrompt: Show how the guide feels by using the map or seed packet. Feeling clue: ____________________.
cards.replyPrompt: Write a follow-up reply where Speaker One uses the clue to make a decision. Reply: ____________________.
cards.reviseLinePrompt: Change this vague answer into a useful one: It is over there. Better answer: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Choose one map clue and write only the answer line. ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add a new question about a different seed packet on the map. ____________________.

cards.title: Rain Gauge Railway Clue
cards.useCase: Use when learners need a spoken line that points to an object clue instead of explaining everything at once: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Read this scene: The rain-gauge railway train waits beside a clear measuring tube. The tracks are dry at one end and shiny at the other. Two rail workers must figure out why the train whistle sounds drippy. Object clue chosen by the group: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a dialogue line that points to an object clue. Do not solve the whole mystery in the first line. Clue line: ____________________.
cards.speakerOnePrompt: Speaker One is the Gauge Checker. Say something about the measuring tube, water mark, shiny track, or dripping whistle. ____________________.
cards.speakerTwoPrompt: Speaker Two is the Rail Signal Helper. Reply with a careful guess based on that object. ____________________.
cards.dialogueTagPrompt: Add a tag that shows how the line is spoken near the tracks, such as called, said, warned, or asked. Tag line: ____________________.
cards.feelingCluePrompt: Show a feeling through movement near the railway, such as stepping back from a puddle, holding up a lantern, or wiping a rail. Feeling clue: ____________________.
cards.replyPrompt: Write the next reply where the Gauge Checker suggests one safe, simple test for the clue. Reply: ____________________.
cards.reviseLinePrompt: Change this flat line into an object clue line: Something is wrong. New line: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Draw or point to the object clue, then write one short spoken sentence about it. ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add one more railway reply that uses a weather word. ____________________.

cards.title: Moss Message Observatory
cards.useCase: Use when writers need the second speaker to react to what was said, not switch to a new topic: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Read this scene: At the moss message observatory, soft green tiles glow with tiny lantern-shaped signals. One observer reads a moss message from the night dome, and the other must react before they decide what it means. Moss signal shape: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a first line and a listener reaction. The reaction should prove Speaker Two heard the first line. First line: ____________________ Reaction: ____________________.
cards.speakerOnePrompt: Speaker One is the Dome Observer. Say what the moss message seems to show. Include the signal shape or glow pattern. ____________________.
cards.speakerTwoPrompt: Speaker Two is the Moss Note Keeper. React to the exact detail Speaker One mentioned before adding an idea. ____________________.
cards.dialogueTagPrompt: Add a dialogue tag that fits the observatory mood, such as whispered, answered, wondered, or said. Tag line: ____________________.
cards.feelingCluePrompt: Show the listener's feeling with a small action, such as leaning closer, touching the moss tile edge, or pausing beside the signal chart. Feeling clue: ____________________.
cards.replyPrompt: Write a reply where Speaker One responds to the listener's reaction and suggests what to check next. Reply: ____________________.
cards.reviseLinePrompt: Change this non-listening line into a true reaction: I have a different idea. Better reaction: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only Speaker Two's reaction to this line: The moss light blinked twice. Reaction: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add one more observatory line where a character reacts to a glow, blink, or hush. ____________________.
